title: Open-world Text-specified Object Counting
property: object count (text-specified zero-shot counting on real images)
why_added: trained text-guided counter tested on held-out FSC-147 classes; named by T2ICount, p. 9
reads: Clean RGB photos in 224x224 windows through fine-tuned CLIP ViT-B-16 patch tokens; one frozen-CLIP text vector enters as keys and values of two transformer decoder layers; never reads noisy diffusion inputs
trained_on: FSC-147 training set of 89 classes with FSC-147-D descriptions and density maps; per-pixel MSE, best of 1000 epochs by validation MAE; no training image has under 7 objects
unseen: yes: 89 training, 29 validation and 29 test classes, stated disjoint (test MAE 15.73); small counts appear only as picked CountBench examples, and no query names a class absent from the image
headline: FSC-147 held-out test classes: MAE 15.73 objects per image with class names and 15.88 with descriptions, against 22.09 for Patch-selection; no-text CounTR is 14.12; FSC-147 minimum count is 7; CLIP ViT-B-16, lower is better
copy_or_avoid: Copy the disjoint split and stitched-image query, adding an absent-class query; avoid FSC-147 labels for a count of two because its minimum is 7, and expect repeated parts such as two heads to be counted separately (inferred)

disagreements.claim: CounTX has CARPK MAE 8.13 and RMSE 10.87 in a cross-dataset comparison with T2ICount trained on FSC-147
disagreements.paper_says: 8.13 and 10.87 come from CounTX trained jointly on FSC-147 and CARPK; trained on FSC-147 alone it scores 11.72 and 14.86 with 'cars', 11.64 and 14.85 with 'car'

disagreements.claim: Xu et al. is the only prior work on open-world text-specified counting, and CounTX is the first single-stage approach
disagreements.paper_says: CounTX does not cite CLIP-Count (arXiv 2305.07304, an earlier arXiv number), which also claims the first end-to-end text-guided zero-shot counter on its p. 2
